caveats: Requires two threads sharing one Timer instance calling scheduling entry points (or ensure_started) concurrently before the timer thread is marked running/alive — unconfirmed library usage.
Relies on threading.Thread.start raising RuntimeError when called on an already-started thread (CPython stdlib behavior outside the tree).
subclaims.reason: ensure_started (celery/utils/timer2.py:110-114) checks `not self.running and not self.is_alive()` at line 111 then calls self.start() at line 114 with no lock held. _do_enter (celery/utils/timer2.py:116-121) calls ensure_started() at line 117 before acquiring self.mutex at line 118, so the mutex cannot serialize the check-then-start. `running` is a plain bool set True only inside run() (celery/utils/timer2.py:81) by the new thread itself, and is_alive() flips only after start(), so two threads sharing one Timer (e.g. the pool Timer at celery/concurrency/base.py:54, reached via enter/call_at/enter_after/call_after/call_repeatedly at celery/utils/timer2.py:123-136 or heartbeat setup at celery/worker/heartbeat.py:52) can both pass the check and both call start(), and the second start() raises RuntimeError. The window spans multiple statements including the is_alive() and start() calls, so an ordinary GIL switch between the check and start() suffices.
